comments.author: @priyeshpatel4382
comments.text: Toxic country for anyone who is not islam - its not a speech, its an observation.

replies.author: @priyeshpatel4382
replies.text: @Outland_US struggling economies unite people of all kinds for betterment, sometimes however people of certain beliefs not necessarily of religion but any belief including religion of same ideology do sometimes unite to eliminate outsiders of their belief in any which way possible including inhumanly even if there was no need to struggle for economic reasons. -( he who had a tooth ache only knows the pain)

replies.author: @Outland_US
replies.text: That is a perspective a lot of outsiders hold based on the headlines. But when you look at the ground reality pure economic survival often overrides traditional divides in the day to day hustle. The country is currently being held together by women in garment factories and a massive youth population demanding better governance. It is a society in extreme transition. Do you think a struggling economy unites people more than tradition divides them?

comments.author: @jacksonmiller9780
comments.text: The fact that this country makes $3 fast-fashion shirts AND $9,000 hand-woven saries that can pass through a ring is the wild paradox I wasn't ready for.

replies.author: @Outland_US
replies.text: It is wild right? The crazy part is that the 9,000 dollar muslin was their original identity before the colonial era crushed it to push cheap textile s. Now the entire world knows them for the 3 dollar shirts. The fact that they managed to reverse engineer and revive the high end craft is an absolute miracle. Do you think the world will ever view them as a luxury hub again ??

comments.author: @LIFEDECODED-b4b
comments.text: Bangladesh is called 'the most toxic country,' but in reality, it's the West that is pouring toxins into it.

replies.author: @Outland_US
replies.text: Spot on. The toxicity is essentially outsourced. Bangladesh is absorbing the heavy environmental cost so the rest of the world can comfortably buy cheap clothes. We offshore the manufacturing and we offshore the environmental destruction right along with it. What would it actually take to force global brands to clean up their supply chains ??

comments.author: @hiddenglobe2901
comments.text: I just checked the label on my shirt. Yupp It's actually Made in Bangladesh. Now I'm wondering how many of us are wearing this country's work right now without knowing. Check your tag and let me know what it says?

replies.author: @Outland_US
replies.text: Love this idea. We are all essentially walking pieces of their economy without even realizing it. Once you know the real story behind those factories you never look at a cheap price tag the exact same way again. Let us see how many Bangladesh tags we can count in this thread!

comments.author: @Investigate_US
comments.text: Having four wives legally is a wild fact! Logically, do you think these deep rooted traditional laws can survive in our rapidly modernizing world, or will they eventually fade away? What’s your take?

replies.author: @Outland_US
replies.text: Great question. It sounds like a deeply entrenched system but modernization is already quietly erasing it. Once women starts earning their own wages delaying marriage and running their own lives the whole dynamic changes. The law might stay in the books for a long time but the practice itself is fading. How long do you think it takes for financial independence to completely rewrite centuries of culture?
